texts: good. the fog and its thinness, the coming-in off the sea, the evening, and day 246 of Year 1 are all carried, and the phrasal verb "came in" is kept whole. The one shortfall is on our side: our day term cannot record that 246 is a day-of-the-year rather than a day-of-the-month, and no rewrite of the sentence repairs that.
good. the fog is reused from the previous sentence rather than re-introduced, the loss of visibility is covered, and the Cliff Path is typed and named as where the reducing happened.

good. Coraline as the keeper, the lantern as what she kept, its link to the Harbor Station, the fact that the burning continued, and the manner "steadily" are all carried; the participial complement "kept ... burning" sits in an unsettled corner of our instruction set, but nothing in the sentence was lost.

bad: "through the fog" was recorded as the *means* by which the lantern produced the light — as if the fog did the producing — which the sentence does not say; it says only that the light travelled through the fog. Rewrite as: "The lantern produced mist-light, and the mist-light passed through the fog." One finite clause per event keeps the fog as a medium the light goes through rather than an instrument the lantern used.

good. the definite "The mist-light" correctly reuses the light introduced in the previous sentence, the nightmoths become a group whose members are typed as moths, and the attracting event is complete.

mixed: the group-level event is fine, but two things go wrong — the threads are marked as *changed* by the leaving when they are only deposited on the lantern, and the per-member rule that a definite plural subject triggers hands EVERY nightmoth the whole bundle of threads, i.e. each moth left all of them. Rewrite as: "Together, the nightmoths left silken threads on the lantern." The explicit "together" makes it one collective deposit and stops the bogus per-moth rule from being generated.

bad: "about thirty-five" has no licensed form for us — an exact count must be a plain whole number and our vague-quantity wordings ("dozens", "several") take no number at all, so the hedge was forced into the count slot as a statistical distribution; and "the next morning" produced only the time-of-day, dropping day 247 / Year 1 even though the passage dates the previous night. Rewrite as: "The next morning, on day 247 of Year 1, Coraline Ash collected thirty-five silken threads from the lantern." If the count must stay approximate, a bound ("more than thirty silken threads") is the licensed way to say it.
